account: It is six in the morning on day 1. I have no confirmed evidence of a secret gathering, though I have lately felt that town business may be happening without my knowledge. I asked about the bakery lanterns yesterday: the neighbour said they were merely welcoming and knew of no gathering. The baker reported steady business, thirty loaves sold by late afternoon, and no new riverside news. On present evidence, the lanterns may simply attract customers; I cannot assign them a hidden purpose. I heard several distant conversations and shouts, including freight, neighbour, innkeeper and builder, but could not understand their words and cannot infer what they concerned. The confirmed business is the builder's bridge inspection report, due today at noon, with two emeralds payable on delivery. The secretary secured the office records and my authorization after I supplied an emerald for a record book. There was confusion about an inn inspection, which the secretary could not confirm; I clarified that none was authorized. My later request to have the builder's report await me after lunch was not heard, so delivery arrangements still need clarification. Today I should read the appointment book, attend the office at eight, inspect grain at the mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, return for council letters at one, take tea with the neighbour at three, attend the office at four-thirty, and be home at seven. I will use those ordinary meetings to learn firsthand what is happening rather than treat rumours or unheard voices as evidence.
